results.quote: For any constant \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists a randomized algorithm that runs in time \(\frac{n^2}{2^{log^{\Omega(1)}(n)}}\) and, with high probability, computes a \((1+\varepsilon)\)-approximation to the edit distance for two strings with total length n.

For any constant \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists a randomized algorithm that runs in time \(\frac{n^2}{2^{\mathrm{log}^{\Omega(1)}(n)}}\) and, with high probability, computes a \((1-\varepsilon)\)-approximation for the longest common subsequence of two strings with total length n.
